messages:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a compact-aware offload admission heuristic. Goal: prefer evicting/staging pages that live in slabs we can compact soon so we don't increase long-term fragmentation when we offload to host. Short sketch below.

jamal: Interesting. Are we making admission decisions per-request or per-tenant window? worried about adding tail latency if we scan slab metadata on the hot path.

maria: Per-request decision but we only consult a tiny precomputed score on the allocation group. score is updated by background sampler. cheap check: `if (tenant.score.compactable > threshold) prefer_offload_pool = COMPACTABLE_POOL`

ryan: Can you paste the pseudo policy? I want to see fallback when compactable resources are exhausted. also how this interacts with bursty small-batch inference.

maria: Sure — rough pseudo: 
```
function admit_offload(req):
  group = req.allocation_group
  compact_score = group.compactability_score // 0..1, updated async
  if req.latency_slo < LOW_LATENCY and req.batch_size < SMALL_BATCH:
    return OFFLOAD_IMMEDIATE // avoid extra checks for hot low-latency requests
  if compact_score >= 0.7 and host_pool.has_space(COMPACTABLE_POOL):
    tag = "compactable_candidate"
    return OFFLOAD_TO(COMPACTABLE_POOL, tag)
  if host_pool.has_space(GENERAL_POOL):
    return OFFLOAD_TO(GENERAL_POOL, "general")
  return DENY_OFFLOAD // let caller fallback to recompute/evict locally
```

maria: The idea is to bias offloads to pages that we'll later pack together during scheduled compactions, so the host snapshot ends up with contiguous free ranges rather than many small fragments.

tina: We should record `admit_reason` and `group.compactability_score` in tracing for each offload. otherwise it's hard to debug regressions. add a tag so Optimize can surface cost vs quality tradeoffs.

jamal: Agree on telemetry. Also: tenant fairness — if one tenant has very high compact_score, they might steal compactable pool capacity and starve others. need admission quotas per-tenant for COMPACTABLE_POOL.

ryan: Good call. Maybe track `compact_pool_tokens[tenant]` and refill on a long window. Low-latency requests bypass token consumption but increment a short-term counter to avoid abuse.

maria: Exactly. Proposal: tokens per-tenant = min(tenant_share, global_compact_capacity * weight). refill interval 1m. Also attach `compact_priority` that background compactor can use to pick victims.

jamal: Complexity note: background sampler computing compactability must be robust under noise — prefer using eviction-age + free-gap-density heuristic, not just hotness.

maria: Agreed — sampler will compute: `compactability = gap_density_score * (1 - recent_touch_rate)` and smooth with EMA.

evictor-bot: [metric] host_pool.COMPACTABLE_POOL.utilization=0.64 host_pool.GENERAL_POOL.utilization=0.81 spike detected 2026-03-21T10:04:02Z

tina: Nice to see a live metric — would be great to add a gated canary for rollout: start with 5% of traffic using compact-aware admission, monitor host fragmentation and tail latency for 24h.

ryan: Test plan: unit for token logic, integration with compactor priority queue (simulate high churn), perf test for per-request cost (should be < 500ns extra).

maria: Rollout plan sounds good. I'll post a short RFC doc with the sampler formula and token parameters. Thanks all — @jamal can you make a quick telemetry dashboard PR? :thumbsup:

jamal: On it. will add `admit_reason`, `compact_score`, `tenant_compact_tokens`, and a fragmentation time-series.

ryan: ping me when the RFC is up, I'll review the compactor priority changes.

maria: sweet — closing thread for now, keeping notes in the RFC.
